checks: The exact five commands retain original launcher and working directory, unchanged subject, declared setup/readback/witness files and saved complete small-output oracles.
Preparation and execution hold the original common mutex; heavy input and static runtime closure verification occur only inside that ownership.
The lock is duplicated to FD>=64 before flock. pass_fds preserves it and child setup checks descriptor device/inode and inheritability before exec, avoiding the launcher FD3 redirection.

The local observer is an explicit derivative of the pinned observer. Kernel identity/RSS/group observation, atomic Popen registration, kill/drain/reap cleanup and signal masks remain reused; exact cwd and artifact directory are distinct.

The complete configuration stderr grammar matches retained UserPreferences source and build-version text. Other cases require empty stderr and exact stdout; workspace failure or unknown diagnostics cannot qualify.
Per-attempt receipts bind command/environment/cwd/FD/parent/birth/PGID, complete stream hashes, normal exit, reaping and empty groups. The first failure stops the serial stage.
Finalization replays exact receipt snapshots, binds the serialized in-memory report, rechecks artifacts after input pins, and checks the named mutex immediately before terminal construction.

Very short native commands may have no live RSS observation. Such captures record null peak and explicit unavailable state; zero cannot masquerade as measured memory. RSS completeness and memory qualification remain false.
No full input N=21, repeated valid timing sample, source-count admission, required-work admission or chart publication is performed by this five-command stage.

locations.finding: The only startup preference file names are preferences and parallel_thresholds; system and user forms are read.
System path uses apl_DIR__sysconf/gnu-apl.d. User paths are HOME/.gnu-apl and fallback HOME/.config/gnu-apl; both alternatives are bound.
Configured sysconf is the retained GNU APL runtime prefix/etc, matching preference_paths.
Both preference readers use open_user_file; no additional XDG override appears in the retained source.
